newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan steelmakers seen maintaining profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: Japan steelmakers seen maintaining profit outlook.

text.p: Japanese steelmakers are likely to maintain or slightly raise their profit forecasts for the 1996/97 business year ending this month, industry analysts say.

"Their forecasts are likely to be little changed as steelmakers already revised down their forecasts in November when they announced their half-year results," said Nikko Research analyst Kazuhiro Harada.
Nippon Steel, NKK Corp, Kobe Steel, Kawasaki Steel and Sumitomo Metal Industries will announce their estimates for parent current profits for 1996/97 later this week.

Based on the forecasts, Nippon Steel and NKK Corp are expected to report a sharp rise in profits in 1996/97 from the previous fiscal year, while the other three are likely to see their earnings trimmed. The steel firms will announce actual earnings for 1996/97 in May.

"The profits of most of the five major steelmakers are likely to slightly exceed their earlier forecasts for 1996/97, helped by bigger than expected domestic demand, particularly a rise in shipments to automobile makers," said Yasuo Fujiwara, senior analyst at Kankaku Research.

Steel shipments are on the rise and the makers' sales volume is likely to be slightly higher than their expectations for 1996/97, in line with higher domestic vehicle production, Harada said. He said steel prices, however, have remained flat.

Japan's crude steel production has been rising since October after falling for 14 consecutive months. Output for the first 10 months of the 1996/97 business year was almost flat from the same period a year earlier at 83.61 million tonnes.
Japan's domestic vehicle production rose five percent from a year earlier to 8.59 million vehicles in the first 10 months of 1996/97, industry data showed.
In January, the Japan Iron and Steel Federation forecast Japan's crude steel output in the year to March 31 at 99.5 million tonnes, down 500,000 tonnes from last fiscal year.
Nippon Steel's actual current profit for 1996/97 is likely to be around its November forecast of 80 billion yen, Fujiwara said. This compares with an actual 64.70 billion yen profit a year earlier.
The actual parent current profits of Sumitomo Metal Industries, Kawasaki Steel Corp and Kobe Steel are likely to be slightly higher than their November forecasts, Fujiwara said.
But Harada expects profits at Sumitomo, Kawasaki and Kobe to be in line with their November forecasts.
The analysts agree that NKK Corp is unlikely to achieve its projected 40 billion yen in parent current profits for 1996/97 because its target was set too high.
NKK's profit will be larger than the actual 1995/96 figures, but it may have to revise down its 1996/97 target, they said.
Nikko's Harada said he expects steelmakers' earnings to improve in the next fiscal year starting in April.

"I am sure steelmakers will post year-on-year gains in 1997/98 profits because they will increase steel exports by taking advantage of the weaker yen and continue their cost-cutting efforts," he said.
Kankaku's Fujiwara also said steelmakers are likely to offset a possible drop in domestic demand by boosting exports.

But Japan's Iron & Steel Industry Federation said it was worried about lower demand from the construction industry due to planned tighter public spending in 1997/98, as demand from the manufacturing industry is expected to remain flat.
It expects domestic crude steel output to fall to 98 million tonnes in 1997/98 from an estimated 99.5 million tonnes in 1996/97.
In November 1996, steelmakers cut their forecasts for parent current profits for 1996/97 as follows, in billions of yen:
November May Actual
forecast forecast year-ago

Kobe Steel 25 40 36.04
